To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ground motion rotational effect is not always significant in nonlinear range and that it is necessary to use MD and FN/ FP directions to rotate the ground motions in order to capture the rotational effect.

the ground motion rotation to MD or FN direction is not always a conservative approach, and the use of MD or FN/ FP directions for rotating ground motions should be based on the results from nonlinear response-history analysis (RHA) of a specific structure subjected to the ground motions.

1) the ground motion rotation angles should be selected to be consistent with the structural response directionality, 2) the ground motion rotations should be based on a suite of motions and not on individual motions, 3) the rotations should be performed to the maximum-direction (MD), and the fault-normal and fault parallel (FN/FP), and 4) the rotation angles should be determined using the linear response of the structure, not using nonlinear response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the ground motion rotations on structural response.
the development of a methodology for rotating ground motions to a consistent direction for nonlinear response-history analyses.
developing a better understanding of the effect of ground motion rotations on structural response, and to identify the best practices in the use of rotation techniques in nonlinear seismic analyses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

rotation of ground motions to MD or FN/FP directions should be performed in nonlinear RHAs for design of structures, and the maximum response values should then be taken from these rotations as the design values.
the rotation of ground motions is necessary for multi-story structures.
the ground motion rotation to MD or FN and FP directions should not be performed without a thorough understanding of the structural system and the ground motions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rotation of ground motions to the MD and/or FN/FP direction should not be considered as a substitute to the use of a suite of ground motion records.
, in general, the rotation of the ground motion to the MD direction provides the most conservative EDPs, while rotating the ground motions to the FN/FP direction is not always conservative.
, the use of MD or FN/ FP direction for rotation of ground motions is not always appropriate, and the rotation to these directions should be done on the basis of the ground motion type.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rotation of ground motions to the MD or FN/ FP directions is not always conservative in the nonlinear response range, and the use of a suite of ground motion records is recommended for a more accurate estimation of EDPs.
rotation of ground motions to the MD direction should be avoided in the design of multi-story structures.
, for nonlinear structures, the MD and FN/FD rotations should be used in conjunction with the as-recorded motions for evaluating the design response of structures.
